fullProfileReview.bilingualParity: The complete German and English expectations, variation axes and both case briefs express the same qualitative scope.
fullProfileReview.scope: Qualitative force balance, declining acceleration, nonzero terminal speed and a changed-drag case fit the current description. Neither case requires a numerical drag law or calculation of terminal speed.
fullProfileReview.case1: The learner constructs force diagrams and a velocity-time prediction and justifies comparison of proposed trends at equal time intervals. Selecting A alone does not satisfy the stated performance. The unbounded continuation in B is now explicitly a proposal, not purported observation.
fullProfileReview.finiteLimit: The case explicitly specifies continuously increasing drag that would exceed constant weight at a sufficiently high speed. Together with zero drag at rest in still air, this supports an intervening positive force-balance speed and the intended stable approach; mere weak growth alone is not used as proof of a finite limit.
fullProfileReview.case2: The increased drag at a given positive falling speed initially exceeds unchanged weight. Upward resultant force and acceleration with still-downward velocity, followed by a lower force-balance speed, are physically consistent. This changes a material model condition and tests transfer rather than swapping numbers.
fullProfileReview.limitsAndSafety: Still air, constant mass and weight and negligible buoyancy are explicit. The task remains an abstract model and asks for assumptions and the extra-force implication of relevant buoyancy; no hazardous experiment is required.
fullProfileReview.coverage: Both content-specific expectations remain required; two independent demonstrations, fresh variation and independent transfer remain required.
